commitResults.messageTitle: Add task storage and list command
Add ability to mark tasks as done and undone
Use a Task class to represent tasks
Extract command handling out of main()
commitResults.messageBody:
main() had grown to 78 lines and operated at several levels of
abstraction at once: it drove the read-eval-print loop, split raw
input strings, indexed into the task array, and formatted output.
This violates both "Avoid Long Methods" and "SLAP Hard" from the
course code quality guidelines, and it forced a reader interested in
one command to scan the whole method to find it.

Break it up into short methods that each sit at a single level of
abstraction. main() is now 17 lines and reads as a summary of the
program: greet, loop over commands, farewell. executeCommand()
dispatches to one focused method per command, and task construction
moves into createTask()/createDeadline()/createEvent().

Three further issues fall out of the same change:

- The "Got it. I've added this task" block was copy-pasted across the
  todo, deadline and event cases. Those cases now share one branch
  that delegates to createTask() and printTaskAdded(), removing the
  duplication ("Minimise Code Duplication").
- A commented-out default branch was left over from Level-2. It is
  deleted rather than carried into the new methods ("Delete Dead
  Code"); git history retains it if it is ever needed.
- The counter named "index" actually held the number of tasks, and
  "description" held a description-and-time pair. Renamed to
  taskCount and descriptionAndTimes ("Avoid Misleading Names").

mark/unmark now use guard clauses so the normal path is not nested
inside an if ("Make the Happy Path Prominent"), and their shared
bounds check is named isExistingTask().

Behaviour is unchanged: old and new versions produce byte-identical
output for a script exercising all six commands and an out-of-range
task number.

The Java coding standard requires K&R brace style: the opening brace
sits on the same line as the declaration, separated by a space. The
four task classes were inconsistent about this, writing `getType(){`
in ten places while Task and Event used `class X {` correctly on
their declarations.

Insert the missing space so brace style is uniform across the
codebase, satisfying the "Follow a Standard" guideline: a reader
should not be able to tell which parts were typed on which day.

Whitespace only; no behaviour or logic is affected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add YuWeiException for invalid user input
commitResults.messageBody: Unrecognised commands were silently ignored, so the user got no feedback that their input was wrong. Catching the exception in the main loop rather than inside executeCommand() means later increments can report input errors just by throwing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject commands with missing or blank arguments
commitResults.messageBody: Typing a command with nothing after it crashed the bot with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and a description of only spaces was accepted as a valid task. One guard method handles both, so each command can supply its own message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate deadline and event argument formats
commitResults.messageBody: A deadline without /by, or an event missing /from or /to, indexed past the end of the split array and crashed the bot out of the main loop. Check each split before use and report the expected format so the user can correct the input.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report invalid task numbers via YuWeiException
commitResults.messageBody: mark and unmark crashed on non-numeric input, and reported an out-of-range number by printing directly rather than through the error path used by every other command. Parse and range-check in one helper that throws, so both cases reach the main loop's handler and printTaskNotFound is no longer needed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject new tasks when the list is full
commitResults.messageBody: Adding a 101st task wrote past the end of the fixed-size array and crashed the bot. Check the count before constructing the task, and build the message from MAX_TASKS so it stays accurate if the limit changes.
A missing space in an if condition, a Javadoc summary without a terminating period, a stray blank comment line, and one error message inconsistent with the others.

All six classes sat in the default package, which does not scale and gives no indication of how they relate. Group them by responsibility: yuwei for the chatbot and its exception, yuwei.task for the task hierarchy. No visibility changes were needed, since the task classes' protected members are used only by their siblings in the same package.
